correctness.rationale: The formal identity \(B_m(q)=(1-q)^{-1}B_m(q^m)\), coefficient extractor \(U_m\), and binomial-polynomial transition give the exact fourth-stage coefficients \(C_1,\ldots,C_4\). The bundled standard-library verifier reconstructs by a distinct exact calculation their polynomial identities over \(\mathbb Q[m]\). For primes \(p\ge5\), the denominator factors are units and \(C_1(p)/p^4\equiv8^{-1}\pmod p\) while the other coefficients are divisible by \(p^5\); for three the coefficients are exactly \((-729,21627,-74358,59049)\) and have minimal 3-adic valuation five. The \(h_1,\ldots,h_4\) first-coefficient matrix has determinant one, and \(B_p(q)\) is an integral power-series unit, so the gcd of every progression term equals \(\gcd(C_1(p),\ldots,C_4(p))\). The fourth coefficient \(C_4=p^{10}\) excludes other prime divisors. Numerical recurrence checks at bases 3, 5, 7, 11 are independent supporting tests, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest exact-progression prior theorem (Rødseth and Sellers 2001) gives divisibility by \(p^4\), weaker at three, and does not determine the quotient residue modulo \(p\). Żmija (2024) introduces the general extraction recurrence and a weaker divisibility theorem, but does not state the sharp fifth-layer prime dichotomy or its normalized quotient law. Sun and Zhang (2017) provide base-digit enumeration rather than this congruence. Targeted published-record and primary-literature comparisons found no equivalent. The result uses prior operator methods, so an unindexed or implicit earlier specialization is a remaining priority risk.
residual_risks: The new exact fifth-layer specialization uses the published extraction method; an earlier unindexed specialization or stronger congruence may exist.

value.rationale: Deep divisibility of the natural p-ary partition function is a documented research topic. This result determines the exact optimal modulus at the first anomalous ternary depth (previous levels 1 through 4 attain their ordinary valuations), detects a sharp discontinuity between p=3 and all other odd primes, and gives an explicit p-adic quotient congruence across infinitely many primes and every index. Its natural prime-depth parameter is not an arbitrary finite slice: depth five is the first exceptional layer. No unproved generalization to other depths is claimed.
